title: Unified metering proxy for multi-source usage claims
creator: Priya Desai
description:
Problem: Usage events come from multiple producers (streaming gateway, batch ingestion job, dedicated node telemetry, and partner connectors). Each source has slightly different shape and idempotency guarantees which leads to duplicate or fragmented token attributions in downstream billing/chargeback jobs. We need a lightweight, highly available service that canonicalizes usage claims into a single canonical event schema, enforces idempotency, attaches provenance, and emits to the canonical Kafka topic used by accounting and billing pipelines.

Goals:
- Provide deterministic grouping keys for dedup and aggregation (e.g., request fingerprint + model+tenant+route).
- Normalize token counting using the canonical tokenizer service to avoid drift between producers.
- Attach provenance metadata for auditability (source, ingestion_ts, original_event_id, schema_version).
- Emit events with exactly-once semantics as seen by downstream consumers via idempotency markers and monotonic sequence stamps.

Non-goals: This ticket is not a wholesale rewrite of existing producers; it is an ingest-time canonicalizer and buffer that reduces downstream reconciliation complexity.
acceptance_criteria: Service accepts events over HTTP+gRPC from all configured producers and returns a 2xx on canonicalization.
Canonicalized events conform to schema usage.canonical.v1 in the schema registry and pass schema validation in CI.
Deduplication reduces duplicate token attributions in the billing pipeline by >95% in synthetic and staging tests.
Downstream billing jobs can consume canonical events from topic 'usage.canonical.v1' with preserved provenance fields.
Canary rollout plan defined and executed with success criteria for latency and error budget (no more than 0.1% errors during canary).
design_notes: Architecture: a small stateless front-end service (Go) plus a horizontally sharded Redis-backed idempotency index. Events are written to Kafka 'usage.canonical.v1' after in-memory validation and tokenization.

Idempotency: compute a canonical idempotency_key = sha256(tenant_id + route + truncated_request_fingerprint + model_version + minute_bucket). Use Redis SETNX with a short TTL (48h) to dedupe duplicates. On collision, merge metadata and return 200 if payloads match within tolerance.

Token counting: call internal tokenizer service (tokenizer.redwood.svc) to compute token delta for common model families; fallback to best-effort heuristic for unknown models and tag as 'estimated_tokens'.
Schema evolution: use schema registry with semantic versioning; include schema_version in canonical event. Producers must be upgraded to include original_event_id and source_type where available.

Tradeoffs considered: RocksDB local index for lower latency vs Redis central index for operational simplicity. Chosen: Redis cluster to allow cross-service coordination and easier ops for short-term TTL dedupe. We'll revisit if write QPS exceeds cluster limits.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): Deploy service in staging, route only synthetic and test producers. Run reconciliation job to compare with current canonicalization baseline.
Phase 2 (canary): Route 5% of traffic from streaming gateway + 10% from batch job to proxy; monitor errors, latency (p50/p95/p99), and duplicate rate in billing jobs.
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): Increase traffic in 25% increments across producers with dashboards and automated rollback on error budget exceed.
Fallback: Producers can be re-configured to bypass proxy with a feature flag. Ensure no data loss window longer than Kafka retention between producer direct writes and proxy-emitted events.
testing_plan: Unit tests for canonicalizer logic and idempotency key generation (CI coverage > 90%).
Integration tests: end-to-end from streaming gateway simulator -> proxy -> Kafka consumer -> billing job simulator to verify attribution consistency.
Load test: simulate peak traffic (2x expected peak QPS) with 20% duplicate storm to validate Redis dedupe and proxy latency under load.
Chaos tests: Redis failover, Kafka outage, and transient tokenizer latency injected to verify graceful degradation and buffering behavior.
dashboards: Grafana: Console / Ingest / Metering Proxy - latency & error rate (grafana.redwood/d/ingest-metering)
